notes: v1b framing-conflict validation set (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-framing-conflict-probe-design.md). two_sided invites both narratives; one_sided_a invokes only the public-safety-regulation framing; one_sided_b only the individual-rights framing. Register-matched analytical asks; balanced, non-advocacy. Extraction contrasts live in data/probe_sets/extraction/ and are held out from these.

prompts.text: Analyze the strongest arguments each side makes about universal background-check requirements for firearm purchases.
Examine the competing arguments each side makes about bans on assault-style weapons and high-capacity magazines.
Walk through the strongest arguments each side makes about red-flag laws that allow courts to temporarily remove firearms from individuals deemed a risk.
Analyze the strongest arguments each side makes about discretionary versus non-discretionary concealed-carry permitting.
Examine the competing arguments each side makes about mandatory waiting periods for firearm purchases.
Walk through the strongest arguments each side makes about holding firearm manufacturers and dealers liable for downstream harm caused by their products.
Analyze the strongest arguments each side makes about arming school staff versus maintaining gun-free school zones.
Examine the competing arguments each side makes about how broadly the Second Amendment should be interpreted.
Make the strongest case that universal background checks are a necessary and minimally burdensome measure to keep firearms out of the hands of dangerous individuals.
Explain the most compelling version of the argument that banning assault-style weapons and high-capacity magazines reduces the lethality and casualty count of mass-casualty shootings when they occur.
Make the strongest case that red-flag laws are a necessary tool for preventing gun violence by individuals who have shown clear warning signs.
Explain the most compelling version of the argument that discretionary concealed-carry permitting allows law enforcement to keep firearms away from individuals who pose a danger to the public.
Make the strongest case that a waiting period for firearm purchases reduces impulsive acts of violence, including suicide, by introducing a deliberate pause before an irreversible decision.

Explain the most compelling version of the argument that holding manufacturers and dealers liable for negligent distribution practices incentivizes more responsible firearm sales and reduces the diversion of weapons into criminal hands.
Make the strongest case that gun-free school zones reduce the risk of firearm-related tragedies on campus by limiting the presence of weapons there in the first place.
Explain the most compelling version of the argument that the Second Amendment protects a right to bear arms that government may reasonably regulate in the interest of public safety.
Make the strongest case that universal background checks impose real burdens on law-abiding citizens without effectively stopping criminals from obtaining firearms through other channels.

Explain the most compelling version of the argument that bans on assault-style weapons and high-capacity magazines restrict firearms commonly owned for lawful self-defense and sport without a proportionate safety benefit.
Make the strongest case that red-flag laws risk depriving individuals of their constitutional rights without adequate due-process protections.

Explain the most compelling version of the argument that non-discretionary concealed-carry policies affirm a citizen's fundamental right to bear arms for self-defense without arbitrary government gatekeeping.
Make the strongest case that a waiting period for firearm purchases can leave a person facing an imminent, credible threat without a lawful means of self-defense when they need it most.

Explain the most compelling version of the argument that holding manufacturers and dealers liable for the criminal misuse of a lawfully sold product unfairly punishes lawful commerce for the acts of third parties.
Make the strongest case that allowing trained, armed staff on school campuses gives schools a means of immediate defense against an active threat.

Explain the most compelling version of the argument that the Second Amendment protects an individual right to keep and bear arms, independent of militia service, that must be protected from excessive regulation.
